proposals.before: Zhu Ergenge, originally named Yougui and styled Baiquan, belonged to the Han Bordered Red Banner and traced his lineage to the Ming dynasty.
proposals.after: Zhu Ergenge, originally named Yougui and styled Baiquan, belonged to the Han Plain Red Banner and traced his lineage to the Ming dynasty.
proposals.reason: 正紅旗 is the Plain Red Banner; 鑲紅旗 would be Bordered Red.

proposals.before: Zhu Ergenge, original name Yougui, style name Baiquan, was of the Han Bordered Red Banner and descended from the Ming dynasty.
proposals.after: Zhu Ergenge, original name Yougui, style name Baiquan, was of the Han Plain Red Banner and descended from the Ming dynasty.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 正紅旗 as Bordered Red Banner.

proposals.before: Su Ling'a on the staff of the Liangjiang governor-general was a fellow townsman and former slave of Heshen who abused his power. Ergenge uncovered his misconduct, reported it, and had him removed.
proposals.after: A gatekeeper of Liangjiang Governor-General Su Ling'a, formerly a slave of Heshen, abused his power. Ergenge uncovered his misconduct, reported it, and had him removed.
proposals.reason: 閽人 means gatekeeper, not that Su Ling'a himself was Heshen's former slave.

proposals.before: Su Ling'a of the Liangjiang governor-general's staff was a fellow townsman and former slave of Heshen who acted tyrannically; Ergenge learned of his conduct, reported it, and had him expelled.
proposals.after: The gatekeeper of Liangjiang Governor-General Su Ling'a was a former slave of Heshen who acted tyrannically; Ergenge learned of his conduct, reported it, and had him expelled.
proposals.reason: Literal misreads 閽人 as identifying Su Ling'a as the slave.

proposals.before: Salt transport was temporarily routed overland, foreign merchant ships were barred from inner harbors, and pirate supply lines were severed.
proposals.after: Salt transport was temporarily routed overland, hongdan ships were withdrawn into the inner harbors, and pirate supply lines were severed.
proposals.reason: 紅單船 are hongdan vessels, not foreign merchant ships.

proposals.before: Salt transport was temporarily changed to go by land; red-banner ships were withdrawn into inner harbors to cut off supply.
proposals.after: Salt transport was temporarily changed to go by land; hongdan ships were withdrawn into inner harbors to cut off supply.
proposals.reason: 紅單船 should not be rendered as red-banner ships.

proposals.before: Kuilun impeached Governor-General Wulana and Governor Pulin, was at once appointed acting governor-general, and presided over their trials.
proposals.after: Kuilun impeached Governor-General Wulana and Governor Pu Lin, was at once appointed acting governor-general, and presided over their trials.
proposals.reason: 浦霖 is conventionally Pu Lin, not the fused Pulin.

proposals.before: When rebels later rose at Baolin Temple in Wan County, he crossed into that jurisdiction and put them down. He then helped the main force destroy Wu Wenxiang at Stone Dam Mountain, drove Lin Lianggong back from Wangniu Pass, killed Lianggong's brother Tingxiang, and received the peacock feather as a reward.
proposals.after: When rebels later rose at Baoling Temple in Wan County, he crossed into that jurisdiction and put them down. He then helped the main force destroy Wu Wenxiang at Stone Dam Mountain, drove Lin Lianggong back from Wangniu Pass, killed Lianggong's brother Tingxiang, and received the peacock feather as a reward.
proposals.reason: 寶靈寺 is Baoling Temple, not Baolin.

decisions.reason: s0145 has 漢軍正紅旗人; 正紅旗 is the Plain Red Banner, while Bordered Red would be 鑲紅旗. The proposed replacement is accurate.
s0145 likewise reads 漢軍正紅旗人; the literal’s Bordered Red Banner is the same 正/鑲 error. Plain Red Banner is required.
s0148’s 兩江總督蘇凌阿閽人為和珅舊奴 makes the 閽人 (gatekeeper) of Governor-General Su Ling'a Heshen’s former slave, not Su Ling'a himself; “fellow townsman” is also unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兩江總督蘇凌阿閽人為和珅舊奴

decisions.reason: s0148 identifies Su Ling'a as 兩江總督 and his 閽人 as 和珅舊奴; the literal wrongly makes Su Ling'a the slave and invents “fellow townsman.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兩江總督蘇凌阿閽人為和珅舊奴

decisions.reason: s0164 has 撤紅單船入內港; 紅單船 are hongdan vessels withdrawn into the inner harbors, not foreign merchant ships barred from them.
s0164’s 紅單船 denotes hongdan ships, not red-banner ships; the proposed literal matches 撤…入內港.
s0203 names 巡撫浦霖; 浦 is the surname and 霖 the given name, so the spaced Han romanization Pu Lin is required, not fused Pulin.
s0010 has 萬縣寶靈寺; 靈 is ling, so Baoling Temple is the correct reading, not Baolin (林).
